text:
asha.infra: heads up, eu-west node pool (A100-80GB) saw a sustained 3x GPU util spike for ~18m, causing tail-latency bursts for shared tenants

kai.sre: saw alerts from prod-bot, digging in now. is this the same NIC hyperburst issue we saw last month?

prod-bot: Alert: gpu-tail-latency-high on dedicated-eu2-s - 1887654305 - affected: 17 jobs - severity: P2

mateo.ml: summary from model-side: a few heavy preparation jobs (data-augmentation pipelines) started roughly same time; they pinned to shared slices instead of preemptible ones. caused KV-cache churn.

jordan.runtime: can we confirm noisy neighbor vs. network egress saturation? I briefly checked pcie/pmu counters and saw elevated DMA stalls on node-23.

asha.infra: node-23 logs show many small allocations + NVLink retries. NIC tx queues spiked but not full. leaning noisy neighbor (GPU memory churn + oversized memcpy).

kai.sre: dumping recent allocs, posting small excerpt:

```
# memory alloc trace (node-23)
2026-03-19T13:21:10Z allocate tenant:ml-prep-job-712 size:14.2GB
2026-03-19T13:21:12Z allocate tenant:search-embed-9 size:3.1GB
2026-03-19T13:21:20Z free tenant:ml-prep-job-712
2026-03-19T13:21:21Z allocate tenant:realtime-gen-4 size:12.9GB
```

mateo.ml: yep that ml-prep job is our batch pipeline accidentally scheduled on shared slice. it should be preemptible spot pool.

asha.infra: why did scheduler place it there? router logs show filter matched fallback routing to shared-slices because dedicated pool quotas were exhausted earlier.

jordan.runtime: ah, quota exhaustion cascade. there was also a regional imbalance in dedicated reservations for eu-west. older autoscaler didn't re-provision quickly.

mateo.ml: cost note: moving ml-prep to spot would cut per-hour GPU cost by ~60% for that job type. but we need to avoid these interfering with low-latency tenants.

kai.sre: immediate mitigation options:
- cordon node-23 and drain noisy tasks (disruptive)
- move realtime-gen tenants to fallback-quantized model on other nodes (lower perf but stable)
- throttle memcpy via nic shaping (experimental)

asha.infra: let's try non-disruptive first: reroute realtime-gen to dedicated-eu2-s-aux if it has capacity, and migrate ml-prep to spot pool. I'll kick the placement change.

mateo.ml: adding a quick check in our job spec to prefer spot and set max-slices=1 for preprocessing: `resources: { gpus: 1, slice_preference: spot, max_slices: 1 }`

jordan.runtime: created routing change: `route: tenant:realtime-gen -> pool:dedicated-eu2-s-aux` (will window for 30s). monitoring now.

prod-bot: ActionTaken: re-route-request submitted by jordan.runtime - 1887654488

kai.sre: after reroute, tail latencies dropped to baseline within ~120s. NVLink/DMA retries reduced. nice.

asha.infra: root cause = scheduler fallback + lack of preempt-preference on ml-prep jobs. follow-ups:
- infra: add a hard admission check so batch jobs with `slice_preference: spot` never land on shared slices
- runtime: expose `prefer_spot` flag in job API (mateo)
- capacity: add warm reserve to dedicated-eu2 to handle 5% spike for realtime tenants (cost tradeoff)

mateo.ml: I'll push a change to our job templates today. small PR to mark preprocessing jobs as `prefer_spot: true` and `is_latency_sensitive: false`.

jordan.runtime: I'll add router rule: `if job.prefer_spot && pool.shared_slice then reject` and surface clearer metrics.

asha.infra: cost ask: what is 5% warm reserve cost estimate for eu-west?

mateo.ml: quick calc: eu-west A100@dedicated = $7.2/hr -> 5% of 200 GPUs = 10 GPUs -> ~$72/hr -> ~$51k/year.

kai.sre: propose compromise: start with 2% warm reserve + autoscaler faster ramp (reduce cooldown to 45s). cheaper and may fix spikes.

asha.infra: ok let's RACI:
- infra (asha): implement admission check + reserve config change
- runtime (jordan): router reject rule + metrics
- ml (mateo): default job spec changes + notify ML teams

jordan.runtime: PRs linked: https://redwood-internal/p/r/3241 (router), https://redwood-internal/p/r/3242 (reject test)

mateo.ml: PR for job templates: https://redwood-internal/p/r/3245

kai.sre: putting a short postmortem note in incidents channel after follow-through. marking this thread resolved for now. :white_check_mark:

asha.infra: thank you. can someone schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to validate reserve tuning?

mateo.ml: I'll set up a meeting.

jordan.runtime: thanks all.

prod-bot: IncidentResolved: gpu-tail-latency-high - 1887655322 - resolved_by: team-runbooks
